newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish share jump 8.02 pct in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish share jump 8.02 pct in heavy volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares recouped a considerable part of recent sharp losses by surging an average 8.02 percent in strong volume on Thursday as political tension eased, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 110 points higher at 1,482, but down from a day's high of 1,502. It had dived 14.9 percent in the past three days.
Trade volume surged to 38.96 trillion lira from Wednesday's 15.20 trillion.
Brokers said prices eased briefly on profit-taking in the afternoon before buying enlivened again. The index was up 8.45 percent in the morning.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan signed on late Wednesday a key National Security Council (MGK) document.

Political uncertainty had mounted earlier in the week due to a row between the coalition's Islamist wing and the secularist military which had warned the government at last Friday's MGK meeting to rein in what it saw as rising Islamist zeal.

"All markets reacted positively to Erbakan's signing of the MGK document. Share prices had become very low, so the news prompted heavy buying, particularly in companies with good 1996 profits" said Gursel Yildiz from Vakifbank.
But brokers said stiff resistance was seen at 1,500 and further progress in Erbakan's reconciliation move with the army and improvements in the ailing economy were needed for an upward trend.

Of the 238 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 228 to six and four were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN leapt 7.34 percent to 1,507, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ soared 9.07 percent to 1,347 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL gained 8.25 percent to 1,575.

Leading actives were largely state-owned firms -- flat steel giant Eregli, up 500 lira at 18,000, oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 54,000 and private utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 17,500 lira at 190,000. They made up 18.4 percent of the total turnover.
